017package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.management;
018
019import java.util.*;
020import java.util.concurrent.*;
021import java.util.logging.*;
022
023/**
024 * {@link LogBackend} implementation for {@link java.util.logging java.util.logging} (JUL).
025 *
026 * <p>
027 * This is the default backend driven by {@link LoggersManager} when no {@link LoggersSettings} declares another
028 * one, and it carries the original v1 {@code /loggers} behavior so the JUL path is unchanged: reads report each
029 * logger's own ({@link Logger#getLevel() configured}) level (empty string when inherited), the root logger is
030 * keyed {@code "ROOT"}, and sets are process-lifetime-only via {@link Logger#setLevel(Level)}.
031 *
032 * @since 10.0.0
033 */
034// Singleton is appropriate for a JUL logging backend — single shared instance per JVM.
035@SuppressWarnings("java:S6548")
036public class JulLogBackend implements LogBackend {
037
038   /** Process-wide shared instance. */
039   public static final JulLogBackend INSTANCE = new JulLogBackend();
040
041   // Strong references to loggers whose levels we've explicitly set.  The JUL LogManager holds only weak
042   // references to loggers, so a logger with no other strong referent can be garbage-collected between a
043   // set and a subsequent read — silently dropping the runtime-configured level (the endpoint's set is
044   // documented as process-lifetime-only) and causing reads to 404.  Pinning here keeps set levels effective.
045   private final Set<Logger> pinned = ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();
046
047   private JulLogBackend() {}
048
049   @Override /* LogBackend */
050   public Map<String,String> getLevels() {
051      var out = new TreeMap<String,String>();
052      var lm = LogManager.getLogManager();
053      var names = Collections.list(lm.getLoggerNames());
054      for (var name : names) {
055         var logger = lm.getLogger(name);
056         if (logger == null)
057            continue;
058         var level = logger.getLevel();
059         var key = name.isEmpty() ? "ROOT" : name;
060         out.put(key, level == null ? "" : level.getName());
061      }
062      return out;
063   }
064
065   @Override /* LogBackend */
066   public String getLevel(String name) {
067      var logger = LogManager.getLogManager().getLogger(resolveName(name));
068      if (logger == null)
069         return null;
070      var level = logger.getLevel();
071      return level == null ? "" : level.getName();
072   }
073
074   @Override /* LogBackend */
075   public void setLevel(String name, String level) {
076      var logger = Logger.getLogger(resolveName(name));
077      logger.setLevel(level == null || level.isBlank() ? null : Level.parse(level.trim()));
078      pinned.add(logger);
079   }
080
081   private static String resolveName(String name) {
082      // The root logger is the empty-string-named logger; expose it under the friendlier "ROOT" alias.
083      return (name == null || name.equals("ROOT")) ? "" : name;
084   }
085}
